Partial rows of a pyramid's mean vectors

Source: R/partials.R
a5_pyramid_partials.Rd

Reduces leaves to exact partial sums at coarse levels, so that pyramids of separate parts of a region, each built alone (a store's partitions), can have coarse levels that span the parts. a5_pyramid_merge_partials() adds the partial rows of every part and encodes the means: the rows that a5_pyramid() gives for all the leaves at once.

Usage

a5_pyramid_partials(
  x,
  ...,
  lods,
  key_resolution,
  weights = NULL,
  weights_type = "uint32",
  types = NULL,
  codecs = NULL,
  threads = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A data frame with one a5R::a5_cell column, an a5R::a5_cell vector, or Arrow data with one uint64 column of cells: an Arrow Table, RecordBatch, RecordBatchReader, Dataset or query from the arrow package. The cells must share one resolution and appear once each; rows with NA cells are dropped. An a5R::a5_covering holds cells at mixed resolutions: convert it with a5R::a5_uncompact() first. Arrow data is read into the engine batch by batch without passing through R, so a Dataset over Parquet files (from arrow::open_dataset()) builds without R holding the leaves.

...

The vector columns to sum (tidyselect, as in a5_pyramid()). Each is reduced by its mean; other columns do not merge and are refused.

lods

The coarse LODs, A5 resolutions below the leaves'.

key_resolution

The resolution of each row's key, the supercell of its cell there: the shard its merged row belongs to. One for every LOD, or one for all, each no finer than its LOD.

weights

The leaf weights column, every weight above zero (a mean over leaves that all weigh nothing has no partial form), or NULL for a weight of 1 each.

weights_type

The type the merged rows store their summed weights in, as weights_type in a5_pyramid(); ignored without weights.

types

Named character vector of storage types for single columns, such as c(red = "uint8", ndvi = "float32"). See "Column types".

codecs

Named character vector of codecs for "mean" columns whose values are codes, such as c(embedding = "aef"). See "Codecs". Default NULL: every column stores its values.

threads

Number of threads, or NULL (default) for a5pyramid_threads().

Value

An Arrow Table in ascending LOD and cell order, with the columns lod (uint8), key and cell (uint64), ncell (uint64), the summed weights named as weights (float64) with weights, and each vector's sums named as the vector (a fixed-size list of float64). Its schema metadata ("a5pyramid_partials") records the vectors' types, sizes and codecs and the weights' name and type, which a5_pyramid_merge_partials() needs: arrow::write_parquet() keeps it.

Details

A row holds a cell of a LOD that has a leaf (the cell containing the leaf's centre, a5R::a5_cell_to_supercell()) and the sums over its leaves: their number, their weights, and for each vector the weighted sum of every element's value. With a codec the values are lifted as the builder lifts them for a mean (for "aef", code * |code|), so with integer weights the sums are integers, exact in doubles below 2^53, and the merged means do not depend on how the leaves were split.

See also

a5_pyramid_merge_partials() to merge them, a5_write_pyramid_level() to write the merged rows.

Examples

library(a5R)
centre <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 9)
cells <- a5_uncompact(a5_spherical_cap(centre, 4000), resolution = 14)
emb <- matrix(sample(-128:127, length(cells) * 4, replace = TRUE), ncol = 4)
x <- tibble::tibble(cell = cells, embedding = emb, n = 1 + seq_along(cells) %% 5)

# two parts, built one at a time
west <- a5_cell_to_supercell(cells, 11) < a5_cell_to_supercell(cells[1], 11)
parts <- lapply(split(seq_along(cells), west), function(i) {
  a5_pyramid_partials(x[i, ], embedding, lods = 10:12, key_resolution = 8,
                      weights = "n", codecs = c(embedding = "aef"))
})
merged <- a5_pyramid_merge_partials(do.call(arrow::concat_tables, unname(parts)))
merged
#> Table
#> 105 rows x 6 columns
#> $lod <uint8 not null>
#> $key <uint64 not null>
#> $cell <uint64 not null>
#> $ncell <uint32 not null>
#> $n <uint32 not null>
#> $embedding: fixed_size_list<element <int8 not null>[4] not null>
#> 
#> See $metadata for additional Schema metadata
